subject: Follow-up: Regional performance & data-jurisdiction checklist
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Cree <samuel.cree@trellishealth.com>, Trellis Health (ops) <opsteam@trellishealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Regional performance & data-jurisdiction checklist

Hi Sam — great call today, thanks for walking us through the Trellis demo and the performance expectations. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope the acceptance tests and procurement path: 

Summary of asks (please confirm/adjust):
- Latency SLOs (P95, inference path, production traffic):
  • US (primary): target P95 <= 90ms for conversational model (chat-llm-v2).
  • EU: target P95 <= 150ms (patient-facing workflows).
  • APAC: target P95 <= 250ms (APAC is lower priority — acceptable to route to fallback if needed).
- Streaming constraints: client expects streaming with token-level flush every ~60ms; tail-p99 streaming latency budget of <= 400ms for UI interactivity.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline concurrency 200 concurrent users, burst to 1,000 concurrent for 15m windows. Typical session token budget ~120 tokens per request.
- Data residency: EU patient records must remain in EU region for both request and logs; US PHI must remain in US. No cross-border replication for EU-domiciled data.

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf (initial SLA language), latency-test-plan.xlsx (test cases / synthetic traffic plan).

Next steps we need from Trellis:
1) Confirm the latency targets above (US/EU/APAC) and any model-level variance (e.g., smaller vs. larger model).
2) Provide the procurement contact and billing cadence for Dedicated/Private discussions (Elaine?)
3) Share a representative test dataset or redacted prompt-set for quality checks (if allowed).
4) Preferred 2-hour window for a live load test next week (suggest Tue 25 May 14:00-16:00 PT).

We’ll prepare an internal test plan and proposal for: Dedicated reserved capacity (if you want consistent P95s), routing plan (primary region routing with APAC fallbacks), and the MSA/SLAs to match the data-jurisdiction needs.

If any of the bullets above are incorrect, flag them and I’ll update. I’ll hold on final pricing until we lock the acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0124

---
Note: redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf attached.
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Regional performance & data-jurisdiction checklist

Thanks Mina — quick notes from infra side: 
- Streaming flush every 60ms is aggressive but achievable if we:
  • reserve CPU pinning on the serving nodes for the streaming worker, and
  • use a smaller batch window for streaming requests (~10-20ms batching).
- For the US P95=90ms target, we should size Dedicated p4-equivalent pool at N GPUs (will calc exact # after we get token distribution).
- Need confirmation if Trellis can accept a warm-up ramp (10–15m) before test window; cold-starts will skew P95.

I’ll draft a short load-test config and attach to the latency-test-plan.xlsx. If Sam confirms the dataset, we can simulate more realistic token lengths and arrival patterns.

-r
From: Samuel Cree <samuel.cree@trellishealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Trellis Health (ops) <opsteam@trellishealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Regional performance & data-jurisdiction checklist

Hi Mina / team — good notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
1) US target: yes, the 90ms P95 is ideal for patient chat flows — our internal UX team flagged anything over 120ms as noticeably slower. We can accept routing-based fallbacks for a small percentage of sessions when you’re constrained.
2) EU residency: confirmed — any request or derived log entries tied to EU patients must remain within EU-hosted infrastructure. I attached our internal policy summary (trellis-data-jurisdiction.pdf) for reference.
3) Streaming: 60ms flush is a guideline — our client-side tolerates up to 80ms, but prefer lower.
4) Procurement: Elaine Brown (elaine.brown@trellishealth.com) handles contracts and PO approvals. Please include her on the next DocuSign.

We can provide a minimal redacted prompt-set (non-PHI) for functionality tests; for perf tests we’ll use synthetic payloads.

Confirming Tue 25 May 14:00-16:00 PT is workable from our ops side — will get Elaine to confirm availability and loop in our security/compliance engineer if needed.

—Sam
Samuel Cree
Head of Platform | Trellis Health
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Cree <samuel.cree@trellishealth.com>, Trellis Health (ops) <opsteam@trellishealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Regional performance & data-jurisdiction checklist

Thanks Sam — appreciate the confirmation. Quick updates and proposed plan: 

1) Acceptance criteria (we’ll include in the SLA draft):
  • US: P95 <= 90ms (chat-llm-v2) sustained for the 2-hour test window after 15m warm-up; error rate <= 0.5%.
  • EU: P95 <= 150ms with strict log/data residency in EU region; no async cross-border log replication.
  • APAC: P95 <= 250ms but allowed fallback to a smaller fast-variant for 5–10% tail traffic.
  • Streaming: token flush <= 80ms; streaming p99 tail <= 400ms.

2) Test mechanics: we’ll run the synthetic load per latency-test-plan.xlsx against your staging endpoints, with 10–15m warm-up, two 30m steady-state windows and an intentional 15m spike. We’ll upload raw metrics and a summary CSV after the run.

3) Docs / legal: I’ll add Elaine to the DocuSign routing. For now I’ve attached the SLA draft; we’ll mark EU data residency clauses as required and add a short audit log retention table.

4) Capacity option: if you want hard P95 guarantees, Dedicated reserved pool is recommended. Monica will outline a couple of pricing flavor options below.

Please confirm the Tue 25 May window; if confirmed we’ll schedule the load orchestration and share the runbook and expected support contacts (SSH jumpbox for test harness, Grafana dashboard link).

Mina
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samuel Cree <samuel.cree@trellishealth.com>, Trellis Health (ops) <opsteam@trellishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Regional performance & data-jurisdiction checklist

Looping in pricing summary:
- Option A (Dedicated - Gold): reserved capacity sized for US P95=90ms, EU mirror, 12-month commit — estimated $33k/mo. Includes 24/7 on-call and quarterly perf review.
- Option B (Dedicated - Flex): monthly commit, auto-scale for bursts up to 1,000 conc., estimated $45k/mo effective during burst months.
- Option C (Hosted + Private routing): lower base cost but best-effort guarantees; suitable if Trellis is OK with soft SLOs and fallbacks.

Monica will prepare a short procurement-ready summary and include potential discount for annual commit. I’ll also prep the DocuSign MSA stub for Elaine.

—Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
